title: Cortical-wide field-of-view two-photon imaging with neonatal AAV injection
author: Oomoto, Uwamori, et al.

steps.title: Pull quartz glass pipettes
steps.instruction: Using a laser puller (settings as listed in the Materials and Equipment table), pull quartz capillaries to obtain a thin, straight, long taper suitable for neonatal skull and skin penetration.

steps.title: Cut and polish pipette tip
steps.instruction: Cut the tip of the pulled quartz pipette to an outer diameter of 50 µm and an inner diameter of 20 µm with forceps and a micro‑forge, then polish the tip with a micro grinder to create a 45° beveled edge.

steps.title: Mark pipette for injection volume
steps.instruction: Mark the pipette shaft at 2.82 cm intervals with a pen. For a 0.3 mm inner‑diameter quartz capillary, a 1 µL injection volume corresponds to a 1.41 cm length; a 4 µL injection volume (used in this study) requires a 5.68 cm length.

steps.title: Prepare double coverslips
steps.instruction: Clean equal numbers of φ4.5 mm and φ6.0 mm coverslips by soaking them in ethanol, then dry on clean paper; place the dried coverslips on a piece of aluminum foil using forceps.

steps.title: Apply UV‑curing resin
steps.instruction: Place a small drop of UV‑curing resin (NOA81) onto the center of the larger (φ6.0 mm) coverslip.

steps.title: Assemble double coverslip
steps.instruction: Position the smaller (φ4.5 mm) coverslip onto the resin‑coated center of the larger coverslip and gently press to eliminate air bubbles.

steps.title: Cure assembled coverslip
steps.instruction: Expose the assembled double coverslip to UV light for 1 hour.

steps.title: Store prepared coverslips
steps.instruction: Keep the cured double coverslips in an enclosed container at 20 °C–25 °C to avoid dust until use.

description: All animal experiments were performed in accordance with the institutional guidelines and were approved by the Animal Experiment Committee at RIKEN. C57BL/6 mice (Japan SLC, Inc., Hamamatsu, Shizuoka, Japan) were bred in our colony at RIKEN and maintained on a 12/12 h light/dark cycle (lights on 8 am to 8 pm) with ad libitum access to food and water. Pregnant mother mice were bred individually in each cage. The adeno-associated virus (AAV) injection protocol can be initiated once the pups are born (postnatal day 0, P0). CRITICAL: All animal experiments must be performed according to the guidelines of the institution. For each step, the type of drug or anesthetic used should be modified according to the applicable guidelines.
